title: What If Yellowstone Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if Yellowstone had a supereruption? It would reach New York, but not how you think.
A supereruption throws out over a thousand cubic kilometers of material. Its last three came about 2.1 million, 1.3 million, and 640,000 years ago.
Near the park, ash could pile up to over three feet deep. Pyroclastic flows would hit Montana, Idaho and Wyoming.
The Midwest would get centimeters of ash. New York and Washington, less than a fraction of an inch.
Even one centimeter could shut roads, short out transformers, and hurt crops.
The twist: USGS says the chance in the next few thousand years is exceedingly small.

description:
What if Yellowstone erupted?
Ash across North America, over three feet near the park, and a very small chance.
